svg.title: Drawing triangles from two angles and one side: exactly one, impossible, or multiple shapes
svg.desc: Panel A: an independently drawn equilateral triangle has two 60 degree angles and each side 4 centimeters, one congruent shape up to turning or flipping. Panel B: two vertical rays perpendicular to the same 4 centimeter horizontal baseline are parallel and cannot meet to form a triangle, so there is no triangle with two right angles. Panel C: two noncongruent 30-60-90 right triangles have angles at corresponding vertices A 60, B 90 and C 30; first triangle AB equals 4 centimeters, second triangle BC equals 4 centimeters. Their corresponding lengths are different because the unspecified 4 centimeter side was placed differently. All coordinate drawings are independent Edulytiks models, not copies of publisher illustrations. Students must draw and measure their own triangles, identify each 4 centimeter side and justify the 0, 1 or multiple result.
svg.text: Given two angles and one side: how many different triangles can you build?
Left AB=4 cm; right BC=4 cm
Original Edulytiks teaching references. The side location must be specified; actual learner drawings require teacher review.
